NAME: Monthly Active Users by Plan
DESC:
A SaaS product logs user activity events. The subscription history is stored as a change table: each row says that, starting on valid_from, a user is on a given plan, until that user's next row. The product team wants the number of monthly active users broken down by the plan each user was on at the time of the activity.

Implement solve so that it returns this monthly report.

Input

events_df

column type description
event_id string event identifier, never null
user_id string never null
event_date date never null

plans_df

column type description
user_id string never null
plan string free text, e.g. "Free", " PRO "; never null
valid_from date first day the plan applies; never null. (user_id, valid_from) is unique

Rules

  1. Re-ingestion sometimes duplicates events. Rows that share an event_id are identical and must be counted once.
  2. The plan of an event is the plan of the plans_df row of the same user with the greatest valid_from that is less than or equal to event_date. A plan applies from its valid_from day included.
  3. Plan names are normalized: trimmed and lowercased (" PRO " and "pro" are the same plan).
  4. If no such row exists (the user is absent from plans_df, or the event happens before the user's first valid_from), the plan is unknown. These events must still be counted.
  5. month is the month of event_date, formatted yyyy-MM (for example 2024-03).
  6. A user who changes plan during a month is counted under each plan for which they have at least one event in that month.

Output

One row per (month, plan) with at least one event, with exactly these columns, in this order:

column type description
month string yyyy-MM
plan string normalized plan, or unknown
active_users long number of distinct users with at least one event in this month under this plan
events long number of distinct events in this month under this plan

Rows are sorted by month ascending, then active_users descending, then plan ascending.

Example

events_df

event_id user_id event_date
e1 u1 2024-01-05
e2 u1 2024-01-20
e3 u2 2024-01-10
e4 u3 2024-01-25
e5 u4 2024-01-30
e6 u1 2024-02-14
e7 u1 2024-02-15
e7 u1 2024-02-15
e8 u2 2024-02-03
e9 u3 2024-02-01

plans_df

user_id plan valid_from
u1 "Free" 2024-01-01
u1 " PRO " 2024-02-15
u2 "pro" 2024-01-10
u3 "free" 2024-02-01

Expected output

month plan active_users events
2024-01 unknown 2 2
2024-01 free 1 2
2024-01 pro 1 1
2024-02 free 2 2
2024-02 pro 2 2

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def solve(events_df: DataFrame, plans_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. Do not convert to pandas, do not call collect() or toPandas() inside solve, do not use Python UDFs.
  • events_df has up to 10^7 rows, plans_df up to 10^5 rows.
  • The returned DataFrame may be empty; its columns and types must still match the specification.

SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(events_df: DataFrame, plans_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # 1. Un événement ne compte qu'une fois (doublons exacts de ré-ingestion).
    events = events_df.dropDuplicates(["event_id"])

    # 2. Plan normalisé (trim + lower).
    plans = plans_df.select(
        F.col("user_id").alias("p_user_id"),
        F.lower(F.trim(F.col("plan"))).alias("plan"),
        "valid_from",
    )

    # 3. LEFT join sur user_id ET valid_from <= event_date : on garde les événements sans plan.
    joined = events.join(
        plans,
        (events["user_id"] == plans["p_user_id"]) & (plans["valid_from"] <= events["event_date"]),
        "left",
    )

    # 4. Parmi les plans candidats, celui dont valid_from est le plus récent.
    w = Window.partitionBy("event_id").orderBy(F.col("valid_from").desc())
    tagged = (
        joined
        .withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(w))
        .filter(F.col("rn") == 1)
        .withColumn("plan", F.coalesce(F.col("plan"), F.lit("unknown")))
        .withColumn("month", F.date_format("event_date", "yyyy-MM"))
    )

    # 5. Agrégation : utilisateurs distincts, événements distincts.
    result = tagged.groupBy("month", "plan").agg(
        F.countDistinct("user_id").alias("active_users"),
        F.countDistinct("event_id").alias("events"),
    )
    return (
        result
        .select("month", "plan", "active_users", "events")
        .orderBy(F.col("month").asc(), F.col("active_users").desc(), F.col("plan").asc())
    )
